evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Joanna: 'in order for me to provide you a more personalized estimate, I just need to ask you some questions about your move. It might take about ten to fifteen minutes if this is a good time.' — Joanna frames the time-box and benefit but doesn't explicitly wait for a clear yes; customer just says 'Okay' and she continues.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Joanna: 'before we start aside from the pricing, do you have any other important concerns that you also want to discuss on this call?' — Asked before probing, customer responds 'No.'
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: N/A — customer raised no concerns in Section 2, so no follow-up opportunity exists.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: N/A — no concerns raised, so no reflection needed.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Gathered: property type (apartment), floors (3rd/2nd), elevators (yes), parking distance (two school buses pickup, drop-off unknown), bedroom count (studio/1BR), items (bed frame, nightstand, boxes, mirror, TVs). Missing: square footage (customer didn't know), drop-off parking distance exact details, number of rooms beyond bedroom count. Roughly 5–6 of 7 items covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Joanna: 'are you planning to pack everything yourself or do you need help with packing the boxes as well?' — Customer: 'I can pack my so[lf].' Asked and declined.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Joanna: 'for the boxes just an estimate, do you think you'll go over 25 boxes or just fifteen to 25 within that range?' — Customer: 'I don't think it'll be over 25.' Asked.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Joanna: 'typically a studio or one bedroom apartment usually takes two and a half to three and a half hours... I'm just quoting it more on the three and a half to four and a half hour mark. Which is an estimated budget of $1,100 to, including the travel fee already.' — Range given ($1,100 to [upper number cut off, but ~$1,300]), typical range provided, but minimal personalization to customer's specific concerns (customer had no concerns raised earlier; minimal call-back to move details).
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Joanna: 'we charge by the hour... $103 per hour, per mover... for two men it's $206 per hour, that already includes the two men and the truck, all the wrap... The only thing outside of the hourly rate would be a one time travel fee of $175... no heater hidden fees... two and a half hour minimum once we go over the minimum, we only charge in fifteen minute intervals.' — Full fee transparency (travel fee disclosed upfront) and commitment framing (2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments) both present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Not asked. After estimate, Joanna says 'Okay' and pivots directly: 'Okay, now typically a studio...' or later 'I can definitely send everything in an email so you have a reference but would you like our help for this move on Friday?' — No 'Does that feel fair?' or pause for customer reaction to price.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Joanna: 'And lastly on time guarantee, if we run late on the time that we schedule, we provide discount for your move.' — Discount terms stated, though brief and vague on exact discount mechanics.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Joanna: 'we will also include other features like our no worries, damage coverage. Which would give you up to $2,000 coverage for any repair, replacement reimbursement for any accidental damages.' — Coverage and $2,000 amount stated, but does NOT explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing, and does NOT explicitly say it's built into the rate (not an add-on).
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No explicit loop-close question like 'Does that put those to rest?' Joanna pivots to the ask: 'but would you like our help for this move on Friday?'
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Joanna: 'any other questions that you might have for us today?' — Empty throwaway phrasing, not the genuine 'What's still concerning you about this move?' Automatically gets a no.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Joanna: 'but would you like our help for this move on Friday?' — Plain and direct, no soft out provided. Customer: 'Yes.' — Full ask without cushion.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No language about 'your rate is locked in' or similar guarantee.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Confirmed: move date (Friday the 9th), time window (8:30–9:00 AM), apartment numbers (pickup 1309, drop-off 1220), email to follow. Missing: phone number reconfirmed, crew size not explicitly stated, crew notes about customer concerns (customer had none, so N/A). Overall missing 1–2 items; partial credit appropriate.

top_strength: Joanna gathered comprehensive logistics details early (elevator availability, parking distance, floor info, item list) and asked the customer's agenda before probing, setting up a structured discovery flow.
coaching_note: Always follow an estimate with a genuine pause and 'Does that feel fair?' question before pivoting to the ask — silence discipline here will surface price objections early and build confidence in the number.
